title: Design & Analysis of Algorithms
subtitle: How algorithms behave, scale, fail and survive

concepts.name: Growth rate
concepts.description: How quickly an algorithm's work grows as its input grows.

concepts.name: Input size
concepts.description: The scale of the problem an algorithm must handle.

concepts.name: Operations
concepts.description: The individual steps an algorithm performs.

concepts.name: Iteration
concepts.description: Repeating a basic operation many times.

concepts.name: Dominant operation
concepts.description: The operation that happens most often and dominates the cost.

concepts.name: Linear time
concepts.description: Work grows in proportion to the input size.

concepts.name: Best case
concepts.description: The input on which an algorithm does the least work.

concepts.name: Worst case
concepts.description: The input on which an algorithm does the most work.

concepts.name: Average case
concepts.description: The expected work over typical inputs.

concepts.name: Correctness
concepts.description: An algorithm must work for every valid input.

concepts.name: Counterexample
concepts.description: A single input that breaks an algorithm.

concepts.name: Vertex cover
concepts.description: The smallest set of nodes that touches every edge.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian cycle
concepts.description: A route that visits every vertex exactly once and returns to the start.
